name: Kingdom of Hungary

areaKm2.note: Wikipedia infobox gives 282,870 km2 (Hungary proper, low); the world_1200 union of Hungary and Croatia measures 369,753 km2 (high). Mid adds Croatia-Slavonia and Dalmatia to the infobox value.

population.note: Infobox: 2,000,000 c. 1200 (J. C. Russell in the Fontana Economic History of Europe). Engel (Realm of St Stephen, 2001, p. 59) gives a density of 4-5 per km2 (low). HYDE/OWID 1200 country series for Hungary, Slovakia, Croatia and Transylvania sum to ~2.4-2.6M (high). Before the 1241-42 losses of 15-25% (Mohi article).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Esztergom, Szekesfehervar and Pest were the only sizable towns; settler "guest" towns small.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing element: royal household and banderium, castle-warrior (varjobbagy) garrisons on duty and the Templar/Hospitaller and episcopal households near the king.

trainedReserves.note: The host that met the Mongols at Mohi (11 April 1241): contemporary sources ~15,000-30,000 cavalry; the Epternacher Notiz reports 10,000 Hungarian dead, "almost the entire army"; other modern estimates 20,000-70,000 (Mohi infobox). The Cuman allies (40,000 people, perhaps 5,000-10,000 warriors) left in March after Koten's murder and are excluded. Counted as levy (nobles, royal servants, castle folk), not standing force.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Household officials, carters, bridge guards.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Free nobles and royal servants owed personal service; peasants rarely armed.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Barons' retinues and knights in Western-style mail; Templars and Hospitallers.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: mail armour and lance, slightly behind German knights.

count.note: Educated guess. Light horse and mounted archers of the old Hungarian tradition, Szekely border guards.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: composite bows, lighter kit than the Mongols.

count.note: Educated guess. Garrison spearmen of royal castles.
Educated guess. Crossbowmen and foot archers.
Educated guess. A few stone throwers; the Mongols, not the Hungarians, used seven engines at the Sajo bridge.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25: Bela IV ignored warnings, the camp at Mohi was a wagon laager left unscouted, and the Sajo bridge was barely guarded (Mohi article).

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25: barons alienated by Bela's revocation of royal grants; the Cumans murdered or departed weeks before the battle.

morale.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: divided realm facing an unknown enemy.

weapons.note: Anchor 4 minus: lance, sword, crossbow, composite bow.

armor.note: Anchor 3-4: mail for the nobility, little for others.

ships.note: Anchor 2-3: Danube boats and Dalmatian galleys of Split and Trogir.

fortification.note: Anchor 2-3: mostly earth-and-timber county castles; stone castles were built only after 1242.

communications.note: Anchor 2-3: couriers; the bloody sword carried round to summon the host.

isr.note: Anchor 2-3: Friar Julian's 1237 reports were ignored.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) Poland 1400 = 956, Turkey 1150 = 743, UK 1260 ~1,290 (2011 int$); Hungary in 1241 was a frontier agrarian kingdom, below England.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Service in kind; royal revenue from mints, salt and settler taxes.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Mining (silver, gold, salt) and village crafts.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Fertile plain, extensive herding.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Remnants of Roman roads in Pannonia; otherwise tracks.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Split, Trogir and Danube river ports.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Dalmatian coastal shipping and Danube boats.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Large horse and cattle herds on the Alfold.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar terrain and local supply; the open plain and few stone fortresses gave little more.

notes: Snapshot = April 1241, between the Mongol crossing of the Verecke Pass (12 March) and Mohi (11 April). Army numbers are the weakest values: chronicles give 400,000 (Juvaini, implied) and Hungarian chroniclers 500,000 Mongols, all rejected; modern estimates of Bela's host span 10,000-30,000+ (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mohi). Per the feudal-host convention the host at Mohi sits in trainedReserves; activePersonnel is the royal household and castle garrisons only. Population convention: Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Dalmatian towns and Transylvania; the Cumans excluded.
